projects.name: Siam Luxe
projects.role: I designed the product structure and user flows, implemented the frontend, integrated authentication and database-backed workflows, and built the admin and QA foundations.
projects.approach: Next.js and TypeScript provide the application architecture; Supabase Auth and PostgreSQL power real workflows; SQL migrations, validation, rate-limiting foundations, Playwright, and GitHub Actions support reliability.
delivered: Orders, reservations, reviews, favorites, and loyalty flows
Member profiles and operational admin tooling
projects.status: The main product foundation is implemented. Live provider setup, deployment, and production operations remain before a public demo can be offered.

projects.name: AI Knowledge Base
projects.role: I built the application structure, protected workspace experience, ingestion pipeline, retrieval layer, role model, operational surfaces, and automated quality checks.
projects.approach: Next.js handles the application shell and server workflows. Supabase provides Auth, Storage, Realtime, PostgreSQL, and row-level security, while pgvector and full-text search support hybrid retrieval.
delivered: Workspace roles, activity logs, health checks, and CI
projects.status: Core product flows are implemented. Live AI answers and semantic indexing require provider credentials; invitation and durable worker-queue workflows remain limited.

projects.name: Nexus Tech
projects.role: I designed and engineered the simulation systems, terminal experience, content model, persistence, campaigns, progression, and release evidence as an independent project.
projects.approach: Python powers a deterministic simulation core, Rich and Typer provide the terminal interface, SQLite stores compatible saves, and JSON keeps scenario content separate from game logic.
delivered: Turn-based company, product, market, team, and finance systems
Offline saves, authored endings, archive progression, and Empire Mode
Reusable scenarios, templates, rival archetypes, and automated CI
projects.status: The local gameplay loop is complete at Stable Alpha. Human playtest sessions and final pacing validation are still required before Beta classification.

projects.name: Finance Dashboard
projects.role: I designed and implemented the frontend architecture, responsive dashboard, transaction workflow, category visualizations, upload experience, and local persistence.
projects.approach: Next.js provides the application structure, Tailwind CSS supports responsive presentation, Zustand manages client state, and Recharts communicates expense patterns.
delivered: PDF, spreadsheet, and image upload preparation
projects.status: This is intentionally a frontend-only MVP. Data is stored locally, while OCR parsing, database integration, and investment recommendations remain future work.

projects.name: Sakura Trails
projects.role: I designed and engineered the product architecture, multilingual content model, search and discovery experience, local-first planner, routing, interactive maps, 3D scene, and quality workflow.
projects.approach: React and TypeScript power the interface; Vite, server rendering, and esbuild produce localized static pages; Three.js creates the seasonal landscape; Leaflet and OpenStreetMap provide consent-based maps.
delivered: Nine regions, 93 destinations, and nine suggested journeys
Search, filters, bookmarks, trip planning, sharing, and validated backups
Responsive images, accessibility checks, Playwright coverage, and CI
projects.status: The feature-rich local-first implementation is complete. A real public deployment URL, native-speaker proofreading, and remaining editorial verification are required before a production launch.

projects.name: Roam America · USA Travel Planner
projects.role: I designed and engineered the product architecture, multilingual content model, discovery experience, state and place guides, daily planner, offline workflow, optional cloud trips, and quality pipeline.
projects.approach: React 19 and TypeScript power the interface; Vite produces localized static pages; Leaflet supports maps; browser storage and a service worker enable local-first planning; optional Supabase services add account copies and expiring shared snapshots.
delivered: 50 state guides, 150 place profiles, and 450 credited local photographs
Search, filters, favorites, comparison, route-aware daily planning, backups, printing, and offline reading
Five-language interfaces, optional cloud sharing, a local Content Studio, Playwright, axe, and CI
projects.status: The feature-rich local-first build is implemented and verified. Public hosting, production environment configuration, and activation of the optional Supabase account services remain before launch.
